* feat(config): resolve settings per variant across DSL and settings file

SettingsResolver layers DSL variant blocks, the global DSL, file
variant.* entries and file root plugin.* keys per setting (first match
wins, no merging), honours preferSettingsFile on every call, warns once
per shadowed file key, and builds a per-variant effective extension.
With no variant inputs the effective view equals the global extension.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* fix(config): no duplicate root parse warning; pin unset-in-block fallthrough

Malformed root plugin.* values are already reported by
PluginPropertiesApplier, so SettingsResolver skips them silently;
malformed variant.* values still warn once. Adds tests where a variant
block exists but leaves the setting unset, and clarifies globalValue /
anyScopeValue KDoc (globalValueOrNull is now callable).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* feat(token): per-variant app token from DSL and settings file

Add SettingsResolver.appTokenFor(ctx, debug): closure, provider, DSL
variant-block tokens (lookup order), defaultAppToken, then the settings
file (variant tokens, then root app_token); preferSettingsFile moves the
file to the front. Warns once when a DSL token shadows a file token.
AppTokenResolver gains additive internal helpers; resolveFromExtension
delegates to them with unchanged behaviour and messages.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* feat(plugin): resolve variant-level settings per variant

onVariants now builds a SettingsResolver lazily (after the DSL block) and
wires each application variant from resolver.effectiveFor(ctx): manifest
task, strip gate + ExtensionsInit (same effective instrumentation view),
mapping/native/bundle tasks, the ndk gate, build-info gate and registrar
excludes. Pre-resolved app tokens come from resolver.appTokenFor. Adds a
per-variant debug line with the masked token and endpoint.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* fix(config): link effective settings lazily; warn only for shadowed variant keys

effectiveFor now links each effective property to its source (global or
winning variant block) and copies only file values that win over the
global property, so DSL values set after onVariants still reach task
inputs as before. Shadow warnings are limited to variant.<name>.* keys,
and the plugin's second parse of bugsee.properties no longer repeats the
malformed-file warning.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* feat(plugin): auto-add modules when any variant scope enables them

Project-level reads that run before variants exist now go through the
SettingsResolver: debug, sdkAutoLoad, feedback and leak.enabled use the
global-scope value (so preferSettingsFile applies), while the NDK runtime
and the compose/okhttp/ktor/cronet module auto-adds, and the Compose
compiler-plugin gates, use any-scope semantics (on if the global scope,
any variant { } block or any variant.* file entry enables them).

With no per-variant input every decision is unchanged; AutoAddScopeTest
pins this against a verbatim copy of the old gate logic.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* test(integration): per-variant settings end to end

TestKit coverage on the two-flavor app-startup-tracing fixture: per-flavor,
build-type and variant-name file keys with lookup order, DSL variant { }
blocks vs file in default and preferSettingsFile modes, the @BugseeDsl
compile-time rejection of global-only settings inside variant { },
configuration-cache reuse and invalidation by a bugsee.properties edit,
unchanged behaviour without variant input, and a late afterEvaluate DSL
value still reaching the mapping upload task.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* fix(config): no probing or early reads without per-variant input

Without preferSettingsFile and without a variant { } block or variant.*
key for the setting at hand, the resolver links (or reads with plain
get/orNull) the global properties, as the plugin did before per-variant
settings: no ExplicitSetProbe, no early provider queries, user
conventions are not flattened. The probe now tolerates final or
disallow-changes properties, and the empty root app_token warning fires
only when the root token is actually consulted.

In Groovy a global-only setting inside variant { } writes the block's own

instrumentation.excludes is DSL-only. Document the no-variant-input fast
path, the settled explicit-set probe, and the token chain's home in
SettingsResolver.

commit.message:
Auto-launch: attach() registers the wrapper identity; opt-in fail-closed filter hold at process start (#162)

* Filters: fail closed after a JS reload until the new runtime installs its filter (#135)

The native network, breadcrumb and log filters outlive a JS runtime, but a
new runtime has not subscribed. Each bridge now tracks whether the current
module's JS armed the filter; attaching a module disarms it, and a request
while disarmed is dropped at once (no emit to nobody, no 9s wait, no iOS
pending-forever). Android log filter no longer resets to the unfiltered
pass-through on module creation, so a redaction the app relied on keeps
applying (dropping lines) until setLogFilter is called again or cleared.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* Filters: arm by module identity, test the constructor sequence, document reload semantics (#135)

Android bridges now record which module armed them and compare it to the
attached sink, so a stale module's late enable cannot arm the new runtime,
and attach() disarms before the sink becomes visible. The log filter's
constructor sequence is a bridge method (attachModule) and is tested.
JSDoc names full reload and OTA reloads, asks for an unconditional
startup call, and documents setXFilter(null) as the opt-out.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* Filters: ignore superseded modules, release the armed module on detach (#135)

Review: a stale module's enable or disable no longer arms or clears the
process-wide filter (Android by sink identity, iOS by the current-module
pointer), and detach releases the armed reference so the bridge singleton
does not pin an invalidated module.

commit.message:
Rebuild query and schema cache files that do not return an array (#2800)

* Rebuild query and schema cache files that do not return an array

An empty cache file, e.g. after a failed write, made every request fail.
With opcache.validate_timestamps=0, the compiled empty file kept being
served even after the file was fixed, until OPcache was reset.

Treat such files as a cache miss: evict them from OPcache, delete them
and rebuild. Also fail loudly in atomicPut() instead of moving a failed
write into place.

commit.message:
Support @skip and @include on the merged field model (#148)

* Split operation codegen into field collection and emission

FieldCollector merges the fields of each operation per response path and
concrete object type, resolving fragments itself. OperationGenerator walks
that model without traversal state, adding __typename during emission.

OperationStack and the duplicate check in ObjectLikeBuilder are gone.
FoldFragments and AddTypename now only shape the document sent to the server.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code

* Send fragment definitions instead of folding them into inline fragments

The field collector resolves fragments itself, so FoldFragments only served
the document sent to the server. Each operation now carries the fragments it
uses, as written by the user, which also lifts the ban on fragment directives.

Changes the document() strings of operations that use fragments.
